Please answer this question with a number--which of the following best apply to the design in the study: 
        (1) totally fun first (i.e., Entertainment game reappropriated), 
        (2) mostly fun first (i.e., design workshop with disabled stakeholders),
        (3) both fun and utility first (i.e., design workshop with diverse stakeholders), 
        (4) mostly utility first (i.e., primary utilitarian mechanic designed first),
        (5) totally utility first (i.e., made by clinicians or specialists, fun incorporated later)
reasoning: The game is explicitly designed as a screener to detect dyslexia, with mechanics and content built around specific diagnostic skills (letter/syllable recognition and phoneme-grapheme mapping). The description focuses on utilitarian screening goals and linguistic criteria rather than co-design for fun or entertainment-first adaptation, indicating a mostly utility-first design with fun layered onto a primary screening mechanic.

        (3) flexible structure with rules (i.e., improv),
        (4) flexible game (i.e., board game with house rules),
        (5) game with rigid rules (i.e., video game)
reasoning: Dytective is a computer-based serious game with fixed mechanics: players must click specified target letters/syllables within a 15-second window on a defined grid with distractors, scoring rules, and level progression. The structure and rules are rigid and not described as modifiable or flexible, matching a game with rigid rules (5).
